# When only ONE side changes a secret, git resolves the object itself and the
# driver is never called - leaving the revealed plaintext stale. The finalize has
# to reveal before sealing, or it silently reverts the change.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

cp base.txt $TMPDIR/base.txt
cp changed.txt $TMPDIR/changed.txt

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

cp $TMPDIR/base.txt s
cp $TMPDIR/base.txt t
exec sesam add s --group admin
exec sesam add t --group admin
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add secrets'

# THEIRS changes s, OURS changes t: both sides move the audit log, but no single
# object is touched twice, so git needs no driver for either.
exec git checkout -b topic
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt s
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'topic: change s'

exec git checkout master
cp $TMPDIR/changed.txt t
exec sesam seal
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'master: change t'

! exec git merge topic -m merged

# Mid-merge the revealed s is still ours - git updated the object, not the
# plaintext, and revealed files are gitignored so nothing else notices.
grep '^BASE' s

exec git commit --no-edit

# Both sides' changes survive the merge.
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/s.sesam
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec sesam show .sesam/objects/t.sesam
stdout 'CHANGED'
exec cat s
stdout 'CHANGED'

exec sesam verify
stderr 'Integrity: ok'
exec sesam status
stdout 'in sync'
! stdout 'out of sync'

-- base.txt --
line one
BASE
line three
-- changed.txt --
line one
CHANGED
line three
